Category.description: Selection slot, not a numeric axis: Economic = one required ranked-weighted livelihood/production trope; Social = one required ranked-weighted community/class/tenure trope; Trait = zero-or-more optional independent ranked-weighted fantasy, hazard/boon, creature, notable-person or historical tropes. The catalog is small by design and tropes should visibly shape urban morphology.

Name.description: Repeatable generic type or trait name (common noun phrase), analogous to a major-work type such as 'mega library'. NOT a unique place name, named monument, named NPC, story title or definite-article epithet. Individual generated districts/POIs acquire their own culturally appropriate instance names during publication.

items.Composition interactions: Crowded-tenement society can make a tight night bazaar, patrician society can build guarded merchant courts, newcomers can run culturally distinct exchanges; optional Veil/ruin/animal traits rearrange access, stalls, safety and specialized goods only when sourced.
items.Core idea: A theatrical fantasy market quarter where caravans, guild factors, haggling merchants and auctioneers compete for valuable frontage and public trading ground; ordinary exchange is always possible, rare/exotic goods require real suppliers.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual inhabitants or visiting traders and reachable suppliers, routes or meaningful market demand.
items.Generative effects: Arcaded market spines, bargaining courts, auction squares, covered bazaars, commodity yards, counting-houses and caravan arrivals; multiple distinctive market/inn/merchant POIs rather than one repeated market token. Principal routes converge on actual destinations.
items.Name: grand bazaar
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor established merchant routes, crossroads, trading agreements, caravan traffic and retained market charters; rising clientele favors monumental auction spaces, lesser trade supports more intimate bazaar alleys.

items.Composition interactions: Patrician estates create elite patron-backed workshops, warrens create dense small makers, guild society shares machines and service courts; ruins supply reused materials and Greenwood/creature traits alter workshop upkeep or siting.
items.Core idea: A district of smiths, masons, dyers, glassworkers, tinkers or fantastical artificers, producing visible craft specialization from actual workers, materials and machinery rather than generic 'shops.'
items.Eligibility requirements: Real productive tradition or trained makers plus usable raw materials, energy/water or supply partners, customers and ground. Magical artificers require real practitioners/medium; ordinary skilled craftsmanship remains available without magic.
items.Generative effects: Distinct forge courts, smoking kilns where fuel exists, open stone yards, dye channels, waterwheel workshops, smithies, apprenticeship halls and shared loading passages. Working-site concentrations shape major service approach and nuisance/open-ground allocation.
items.Name: artificer quarter
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Prefer available stone/wood/metal/textile inputs, guild or workshop ties, water/fuel/transport, clientele and credible productive specialties; downweight expensive residential frontages without suppliers.

items.Composition interactions: Guild commons can manage tolls and warehouses, patricians may privatize quays, warrens crowd behind dock walls; old walls and Veil discontinuities produce distinctive choke points without invented cargo or portals.
items.Core idea: The noisy transfer ward for caravans, pack beasts, cargo boats and heavy freight, with guarded arrival courts and goods moving between transport modes.
items.Eligibility requirements: A connected regional road, landing, harbor, canal or other genuine freight transfer and goods flow.
items.Generative effects: Broad enclosed caravanserai yards, weighing houses, guarded warehouses, towpaths, cargo cranes where built and feasible, stock pens, toll and customs courts and large freight approaches; river quays only where water/shore supports them.
items.Name: caravanserai and quays
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Weight actual caravan intersections, maintained regional roads, navigable waterfront or portage, reliable freight flows and access to city gates; an inland caravanserai is legitimate without a quay.

items.Composition interactions: Warrens produce packed food stalls and tenement bakehouses, patrician estates sponsor walled granaries and provision gardens; beast rookeries, springs, floods and old walls change sanitation, storage and access.
items.Core idea: The city's food-making underbelly: millers, butchers, bakers, brewers, fishmongers and grain factors, fed by real rural or imported supply rather than a generic food-services label.
items.Eligibility requirements: Reachable food or arable/working land, water where needed, and actual provisioning demand.
items.Generative effects: Granary towers, milling courts, smokehouses, ovens, slaughter yards and crowded produce markets where supplies justify them; noisy service lanes, protected water/food storage and productive POIs differentiate the quarter.
items.Name: granary quarter
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor active rural provisioning roads, granaries, slaughter and processing capability, rivers or wells where necessary, cultivated fringes, fish landings or imported food corridors; do not assume every food trade needs waterfront.

items.Composition interactions: With exiles the hostel becomes an arrival neighborhood; with patricians it becomes fashionable bathhouses and guest compounds; with crowded warrens it becomes cramped lodging and shared kitchens. A famous resident or haunted ruin changes who visits.
items.Core idea: A fantasy city's living hospitality district: inns, bathhouses, boarding halls, healers, hostels, cooks and small household trades serve locals, travelers and the unlucky.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual settled population, available housing/built stock and reachable basic supplies/services.
items.Generative effects: Lantern-lit inn courts and lodging clusters, bath and laundry grounds where water exists, healer yards, communal kitchens, traveler stables and boarding courtyards; prominent inns and public service POIs become actual routes and places.
items.Name: inn quarter
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor real occupied residents, arrival ways, pilgrimage/market visitors, safe approach routes and gaps in hospitality or household services. Offers a viable ordinary livelihood without automatically inventing a rare institution.

items.Composition interactions: Guild governance produces schools and craft patents, patricians private salons, warrens cheap copyists' alleys, ruins archive-hunting scholars, and an actual Veil/Salt/Aurora phenomenon may change studies without authoring new magic.
items.Core idea: An enclave of scribes, astrologers where supported, cartographers, physicians, apothecaries, tutors and archive keepers, whose patronage and knowledge can physically dominate a district.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual schools, patrons, learning tradition, archive, medical needs or equivalent documented expertise; magical services require real practitioners/medium.
items.Generative effects: Scriptorium courts, archive cloisters, herb gardens, apothecary lanes, public disputation squares, observatory courtyards where commissioned and medical halls. Diverse specialized POIs require independent evidence, not cloned academies.
items.Name: scribe and apothecary quarter
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor known libraries, schools, magical/medical training where supported, record-keeping courts, patrons, literacy, rare ingredients and actual clients; lacking those, substantial scholarly complexes are ineligible.

items.Composition interactions: Grand Bazaar yields bazaar-warrens; Scriptoria supports cramped copyist lodgings; the old city wall may confine or divide houses; creatures, floodwater and Greenwood create distinct burdened or celebrated warrens.
items.Core idea: An iconic crush of tightly inhabited courts, improvised additions, shared resources and contested passage: a social morphology of crowding, not an automatic morality or crime label.
items.Eligibility requirements: Occupied population, limited housing/land and credible crowding or low-capital conditions.
items.Generative effects: A visibly knotted dense district with small shared courts, interlocking upper structures at Street detail, roof passages where viable, narrow service gaps and intense localized demand for markets, baths and water points; keep real through-access.
items.Name: tenement warrens
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor actual high occupancy relative to viable space, low investment or constrained tenure, high employment accessibility and limited expansion room; crowding does not prove slum poverty or criminality.

items.Composition interactions: Freight gives private merchant dynasties and warehouses, Scriptoria gives patronized scholars, arts/crafts give luxury workshops; ruins or Veil hazards become private guarded landmarks rather than vanishing.
items.Core idea: A landscape of powerful families, luxurious estates, controlled gates, retainers and rival household compounds—where actual status or patronage can afford visible space.
items.Eligibility requirements: Existing substantial wealth, tenure, political privilege or sponsor relationships that can support reserved land.
items.Generative effects: Walled or hedged manor precincts, formal gardens, long approach avenues, household chapels, family courts, private groves and conspicuous gaps between compounds. Splendid but deliberately low-coverage urban land distinguishes the district.
items.Name: noble estates
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor demonstrable wealth, political privilege, ancestral tenure, court patrons or strongly supported high-value holdings; do not assign aristocracy because a City template has a grand style.

items.Composition interactions: Bazaar + Guildholds becomes competing auction halls, Freight becomes a convoy league, Food yields bakers' and millers' guild courts; old ruins and fantastical traits can change oaths, shared equipment and property rules without free magic.
items.Core idea: Corporations and brotherhoods govern shared courtyards, negotiated rights and collective services under binding charters or guild oaths.
items.Eligibility requirements: Grounded guild/trade institutions, common workshop services or durable cooperative rights.
items.Generative effects: Grand guildhall commons, workshops sharing guarded courtyards, processional guild banners/routes, competing chapterhouses, shared reservoirs or machinery and conspicuous rights boundaries between guild compounds.
items.Name: guild commons
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor established guilds, ward charters, long-lived productive ties, common machinery or genuine corporate rights, rather than assuming every workshop district is guild-controlled.

items.Composition interactions: Outlanders trading in a bazaar generate diplomatic markets, artisans carry skills, innkeepers receive pilgrims; economic wealth and actual inherited rights determine whether it is elite, cramped or communal. A famous NPC could anchor an existing refuge.
items.Core idea: An arrival community of refugees, migrants, traveling peoples or exiles maintaining distinct customs, meeting places and internal routes, sometimes wealthy, sometimes struggling, never automatically a ghetto.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual immigration, displacement, trade-connected visiting communities or documented resident contacts; do not assume migrants are poor or unwanted.
items.Generative effects: Threshold squares, hostels, culturally distinct gathering courts, clustered family yards, guest markets, memorials or temples where real practices exist, and routes linking arrival roads to deeper neighborhood homes.
items.Name: outlander enclave
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor actual migration, displacement, established diaspora links, caravan visitors, multilingual/cultural contact and supported communal rights; without outsiders or contacts this trope is ineligible.

items.Composition interactions: An artisan Freefolk ward shares workyards, a market quarter bargains over stall rights, a freight ward controls public tolls; a spring or ancient ruin can become a protected communal site and an outgrown wall a shared promenade.
items.Core idea: A self-governing ward of independent households, mutual defense and open commons, held together by assemblies, charters or hard-won freedoms rather than wealth or aristocratic patronage.
items.Eligibility requirements: Established civilian households or community rights with legal/social support; no invented charter or polity.
items.Generative effects: Large deliberately open assembly greens, public meeting halls, shared mills or wells, freely connected pedestrian approaches and defensible yet publicly accessible ward edges; contrasts with private estates and enclosed guildholds.
items.Name: freehold commons
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor actual chartered rights, communal practices, independent household tenure, historical popular assemblies or supported sanctuary/refuge agreements; cannot invent a revolution.

items.Composition interactions: A bazaar gains peculiar unloading/inspection courts if a real stable connection exists; the Warrens crowd around hazardous shortcuts; Highborn Courts may gate dangerous ground. Do not author a new Veil link or practitioners from a trait selection.
items.Core idea: A rip, fold, unreachable near-place or unstable seam in the Veil is woven through the district's daily routes, fortunes and fears; only real, maintained paired doors enable reliable passage.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual Veil medium/discontinuity in inherited physical/magical state; stable travel only with established paired destinations/keepers.
items.Generative effects: Bent destination approaches, dead-end courts facing impossible thresholds, guarded waiting yards, displaced frontage, alternate routes and actual obstruction/refuge POIs. Seam geometry should change City access and land demand, not merely decorate a map with purple magic.
items.Name: Veil tear
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Increase weight near real Veil features, supported maintainers and meaningful route/terrain interference.

items.Composition interactions: Freefolk can protect sacred/public groves, guilds bargain for access, and a merchant quarter may lose or gain an intimate covered arcade. Actual Greenwood media and rooted vegetation must be the cause.
items.Core idea: An old quarter is being entangled, sheltered or consumed by Greenwood growth that competes with stone, roofs and human tenure.
items.Eligibility requirements: Real Greenwood influence plus viable rooting/water/ecological substrate and local history.
items.Generative effects: Tree-swallowed courtyards, interrupted alleys, root-lifted masonry, canopy passages, protected living greens and abandoned lanes where real roots, water and magical exposure support them.
items.Name: Greenwood encroachment
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor old gardens, water and maintained or abandoned structures with Greenwood signals.

items.Composition interactions: Scriptoria copy testimony, guilds maintain shrines and patricians defend family crypts; a crowded market may press against sacred empty land, but no dead are raised and no new Salt field is created.
items.Core idea: Preserved ancestors, bone courts and record-keeping funerary custodians sit beside the living, changing rights to some of the city's most valuable ground.
items.Eligibility requirements: Real burial/history, Salt-bearing preservation or cultural custodianship where appropriate; no invented necropolis.
items.Generative effects: Ossuary terraces, narrow processional approaches, preserved memorial facades, burial courts and no-build sanctums with real retained remains. Where Salt phenomena matter, provide their preserving/corrosive obligations via the magic owner.
items.Name: Salt ossuary
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor extant old burial sites, grave stewardship, memorial routes and preserved material.

items.Composition interactions: Tenement residents improvise elevated commons while wealthy courts fund raised approaches; a freight district moves loading toward deeper shore. Do not conjure a flood on dry high ground or replay global erosion.
items.Core idea: The quarter lives with recurring water, silt and drowned former streets; practical boats, raised thresholds and abandoned lower levels become common where hydrology supports them.
items.Eligibility requirements: Low/wet basin, floodplain or documented water hazard; not chosen for dry high ground.
items.Generative effects: Curved embankment roads, elevated causeways, ferry stairs, canal yards, water-stained old walls and flood-abandoned precinct edges. Some claimed open ground becomes wet greens or working marsh, not generic undeveloped pixels.
items.Name: flooded lanes
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor connected floodplains, channels, tidal outlets, actual historic flood risk.

items.Composition interactions: Guildholds may meter water, Freefolk protect a commons, noble families enclose gardens, and food makers establish viable mills only with sufficient flow. A magical blessing is optional and requires genuine magical evidence.
items.Core idea: An actual perennial source of water becomes a fiercely valued district heart, treasured as a blessing whether or not it possesses any magic.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual spring/groundwater-fed water availability and viable access/rights; supernatural healing is not implied.
items.Generative effects: A spring-fed public fountain, baths, guarded channels, orchard gardens, laundry courts and road approaches converging on the water; its real catchment and use rights become spatial constraints.
items.Name: perennial spring
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor real water sources, historical supply disputes, cultivation or crafts requiring dependable water.

items.Composition interactions: Markets exploit vault entrances, residents build over secure masonry, scholars seek records and elites preserve stone terraces; the underlying historical structures must exist or be resolved from legitimate provenance.
items.Core idea: Older ruins persist as steps, crypt vaults, buried lanes and reused halls beneath an occupied quarter, making present streets follow inconvenient ancient stone.
items.Eligibility requirements: Retained existing ruins, recorded ancient works or credible historical material evidence.
items.Generative effects: Crooked roads around exposed foundations, monumental roofless courts, walled excavations, repurposed aqueduct galleries and ruin-linked POIs whose identities survive successive settlement phases.
items.Name: buried ruins
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor known older ruins and reused infrastructure, old tombs or abandoned city strata.

items.Composition interactions: Artisans quarry masonry, highborn courts convert towers, bazaar traders crowd old gates and Freefolk establish common walks. The wall requires an actual supported older construction history and isn't the current city stencil.
items.Core idea: A crumbling old defensive perimeter and its gate passages divide what is now an ordinary interior neighborhood, with fragments still governing property, traffic and memory.
items.Eligibility requirements: An actual inherited/locally modeled former wall, gate alignment or fortification history.
items.Generative effects: Broken gatehouses used as markets, internal masonry arcs, odd road bends at old portals, vanished stretches reused as promenades and defensible towers occupied by new users; visible condition changes across historical phases.
items.Name: outgrown city wall
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor formerly protected cores and phases of outward settlement growth.

items.Composition interactions: Markets may sell to admirers, craftsmen receive commissions, tenements offer protection, and nobles contest prestige. The person and their social role must originate from actual named history; the trait cannot invent a celebrity.
items.Core idea: A truly notable and geographically situated person, creature-tamer, ruler-in-exile, champion, scholar or notorious patron makes one lane or precinct famous across the city.
items.Eligibility requirements: Existing named/recorded NPC or supported notable-person event plus a persistent plausible home/role, not an invented public figure.
items.Generative effects: A distinctive named residence or working hall, pilgrimage/visitor routes, guarded thresholds or patronized facilities appropriate to that NPC's actual role, along with rumor or fame-centered landmark identity.
items.Name: notable resident
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor actual residence, patrons, guild authority, scholarship, services or notable historical site.

items.Composition interactions: Forgeways may dislike heat-loving beasts, the Warrens shelter from swarms, Highborn Courts keep display roosts and Freefolk protect a nesting green. Species, breeding and habitat remain controlled by ecology, not selected out of thin air.
items.Core idea: A spectacular rookery, den or herd of real native or fantastical creatures occupies city cliffs, towers, warm chimneys or sacred treetops, to residents' delight or fury.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual animal species/habitat or magical ecology and nesting/food substrate supported by the world.
items.Generative effects: Roost-scarred towers, protected nesting cliffs, animal-feeding squares, no-build buffer grounds, droppings/nuisance corridors and unusual keeper or animal-trade POIs if actual occupation supports them.
items.Name: creature rookery
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor connected roofs, cliffs, groves, refuse/food sources or protected breeding grounds.
